questions.q: What is the third water feature found in the wetland habitat at Hinchingbrooke Country Park? (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

The park has various habitats including wetland, grassland and woodland. The wetland area contains lakes, ponds and one other water feature.
questions.explanation: The wetland area contains lakes, ponds, and a **stream**. This tests vocabulary related to natural water features. 'Stream' /striːm/ = a small, narrow river.

questions.q: In Science lessons at the park, children look at ___ about plants. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

During educational visits, children study several subjects. In **Science**, they examine something specific about plants.
questions.explanation: Children examine **cycles** about plants (e.g., life cycles, growth cycles). The word 'cycles' /ˈsaɪklz/ refers to recurring sequences of events — a key Science concept.

questions.q: In Geography lessons, children learn to use a ___ and compass. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

In **Geography** lessons, children learn to use a navigation tool along with a compass.
questions.explanation: Children learn to use a **map** and compass. A map /mæp/ is a diagrammatic representation of an area. Common collocation: 'read a map', 'map-reading skills'.

questions.q: The Leisure and Tourism subject mostly concentrates on the park's ___. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

In **Leisure and Tourism**, the subject mostly concentrates on one particular aspect of the park.
questions.explanation: Leisure and Tourism focuses on the park's **facilities** — the amenities and services available. 'Facilities' /fəˈsɪlɪtiz/ = things that make it easier to do something or that are provided for a particular purpose.

questions.q: In Music lessons, children make ___ with natural materials. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

In **Music** lessons, children create something using natural materials and also experiment with rhythm and speed.
questions.explanation: Children make **sounds** with natural materials. This is a listening-based inference question. 'Sounds' /saʊndz/ — note: 'instruments' could seem plausible but the audio context specifies 'sounds' as the answer here.

questions.q: Outdoor educational visits give children a feeling of ___ that they may not have elsewhere. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

Outdoor educational visits provide children with a feeling they may not have elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Visits give children a feeling of **freedom** /ˈfriːdəm/ — the sense of being unrestricted. This is an affective/emotional vocabulary item common in IELTS Listening Part 1.

questions.q: Children learn new ___ and gain self-confidence during outdoor educational visits. (Write ONE WORD)
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

Beyond emotional benefits, children also develop something practical during outdoor visits.
questions.explanation: Children learn new **skills** /skɪlz/ and gain self-confidence. Common collocation: 'develop skills', 'build skills'. Distinguishing 'skills' from 'knowledge' is a typical IELTS precision task.

questions.q: Which group of adults is specifically mentioned as attending free of charge?
questions.passage:
**Hinchingbrooke Country Park – Part 1 (Questions 1–10)**

There is a cost per child for the educational visit. Adults such as one specific group attend for free.
questions.explanation: **Parents** are mentioned as attending free. This is a detail-recognition question. In IELTS Listening, distractors like 'teachers' may also seem plausible — careful listening/reading is required.

questions.q: During the visit to Malatte, France, members especially enjoyed:
questions.passage:
**Stanthorpe Twinning Association – Part 2 (Questions 11–15)**

During the visit to Malatte in France, members had various experiences.
questions.explanation: Members especially enjoyed **experiencing a river trip** (Option B). This is a multiple-choice question where all three options may be mentioned in the audio, but only one is described as especially enjoyable. Key skill: distinguishing degree of enjoyment.

questions.q: What will happen in Stanthorpe to mark the 25th anniversary of the Twinning Association?
questions.passage:
**Stanthorpe Twinning Association – Part 2 (Questions 11–15)**

The Association is marking its 25th anniversary with a specific event or installation in Stanthorpe.
questions.explanation: **A tree will be planted** (Option A). Anniversary commemorations often appear in IELTS Listening. Note the difference between 'planted' (permanent, living) vs. 'bought' or 'built' — the audio confirms planting.
options: A garden seat will be bought.

questions.q: Which event raised the MOST funds this year?
questions.passage:
**Stanthorpe Twinning Association – Part 2 (Questions 11–15)**

The Association raised funds through several events this year.
questions.explanation: **The cookery demonstration** (Option C) raised the most funds. Superlative comparison questions ('most') require careful attention to comparative language in the audio (e.g., 'raised more than', 'topped the list').

questions.q: For the first evening with French visitors, host families are advised to:
questions.passage:
**Stanthorpe Twinning Association – Part 2 (Questions 11–15)**

Host families are given advice about what to do on the first evening with French visitors.
questions.explanation: Host families are advised to **have a meal at home** (Option C). This is a practical instruction question. The word 'advised' signals a recommendation — key listening vocabulary: 'we suggest', 'it's best to', 'we recommend'.
options: take them for a walk round the town

questions.q: On Saturday evening, there will be the chance to:
questions.passage:
**Stanthorpe Twinning Association – Part 2 (Questions 11–15)**

The Saturday evening programme includes a specific activity for visitors.
questions.explanation: Visitors can **take part in a competition** (Option C). 'Take part in' /teɪk pɑːt ɪn/ is a phrasal verb meaning to participate. Common IELTS collocation: 'take part in an event/activity/competition'.

questions.q: Which TWO things did Colin find most satisfying about his bread reuse project?
questions.passage:
**Colin's Bread Reuse Project – Part 3 (Questions 21–22)**

Colin reflects on what he found most satisfying about his bread reuse project. Two aspects stood out for him.

Options:
- A: receiving support from local restaurants
- B: finding a good way to prevent waste
- C: overcoming problems in a basic process
- D: experimenting with designs and colours
- E: learning how to apply 3-D printing
questions.explanation: Colin found **B (finding a good way to prevent waste)** and **C (overcoming problems in a basic process)** most satisfying. 'Most satisfying' implies deep personal fulfilment — listen for emotional language like 'really pleased', 'proud of', 'what I valued most'.

questions.q: Which TWO ways do the students agree that touch-sensitive food label sensors could be developed in future?
questions.passage:
**Touch-Sensitive Sensors for Food Labels – Part 3 (Questions 23–24)**

Two students discuss future development possibilities for touch-sensitive sensors used on food labels.

Options:
- A: for use on medical products
- B: to show that food is no longer fit to eat
- C: for use with drinks as well as foods
- D: to provide applications for blind people
- E: to indicate the weight of certain foods
questions.explanation: The students agree on **B (to show food is no longer fit to eat)** and **D (to provide applications for blind people)**. Key skill: distinguishing personal opinion ('I think') from mutual agreement ('we both agree', 'yes, that too'). 'Fit to eat' = safe/suitable for consumption.

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about the **use of local products** (Question 25)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Students share opinions on food trends. Match each trend to the correct opinion:

| Letter | Opinion |
|--------|------------------|
| A | Only relevant to young people |
| B | May have disappointing results |
| C | Already seems widespread |
| D | Retailers should do more |
| E | More financial support needed |
| F | Most people know little about this |
| G | Stricter regulations needed |
| H | Could be dangerous |
questions.explanation: The opinion for **use of local products** is **D – Retailers should do more to encourage this**. 'Local products' /ˈloʊkəl ˈprɒdʌkts/ = goods produced in the nearby area. Common collocation: 'locally sourced', 'buy local'.
options: A – Only relevant to young people
C – Already seems to be widespread
D – Retailers should do more to encourage this
E – More financial support is needed

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about **reduction in unnecessary packaging** (Question 26)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Same opinion bank as above (A–H).
questions.explanation: The opinion for **reduction in unnecessary packaging** is **G – There should be stricter regulations about this**. 'Packaging' /ˈpækɪdʒɪŋ/ = materials used to wrap products. Key collocation: 'reduce packaging', 'single-use packaging', 'packaging regulations'.
options: C – Already seems to be widespread
G – There should be stricter regulations

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about **gluten-free and lactose-free food** (Question 27)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Same opinion bank as above (A–H).
questions.explanation: The opinion is **C – Already seems to be widespread**. 'Gluten-free' /ˈɡluːtən friː/ and 'lactose-free' /ˈlæktoʊs friː/ refer to foods without specific proteins/sugars. These dietary categories are now common in mainstream supermarkets.
options: A – Only relevant to young people
C – Already seems to be widespread
F – Most people know little about this

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about **use of branded products related to celebrity chefs** (Question 28)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Same opinion bank as above (A–H).
questions.explanation: The opinion is **B – May have disappointing results**. 'Branded products' /ˈbrænd ɪd ˈprɒdʌkts/ = items sold under a famous name. The students suggest celebrity chef branding may not live up to expectations — a form of critical consumer commentary.
options: A – Only relevant to young people
E – More financial support is needed

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about the **development of 'ghost kitchens' for takeaway food** (Question 29)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Same opinion bank as above (A–H).
questions.explanation: The opinion is **F – Most people know little about this**. 'Ghost kitchens' /ɡoʊst ˈkɪtʃɪnz/ (also called dark kitchens) are delivery-only restaurant facilities with no dine-in option — a relatively new and unfamiliar concept to the general public.
options: C – Already seems to be widespread
F – Most people know little about this

questions.q: What is the students' opinion about the **use of mushrooms for common health concerns** (Question 30)?
questions.passage:
**Food Trends – Part 3 (Questions 25–30)**

Same opinion bank as above (A–H).
questions.explanation: The opinion is **H – This could be dangerous**. The use of medicinal or functional mushrooms is a growing wellness trend, but the students express concern about safety — particularly unsupervised use. 'Dangerous' /ˈdeɪndʒərəs/ = likely to cause harm.
options: E – More financial support is needed
F – Most people know little about this

questions.q: In the 1930s, a local teacher realised that stones beneath the bog surface were once ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

Ceide Fields is an important Neolithic archaeological site in northwest Ireland.

In the 1930s, a local teacher noticed that stones buried beneath the bog had once served a particular purpose.
questions.explanation: The stones were once **walls** — part of ancient field boundaries. 'Walls' /wɔːlz/ in an archaeological context often refers to stone enclosures or boundaries. Key vocabulary: 'dry-stone walls', 'field walls', 'boundary walls'.

questions.q: The teacher's ___ became an archaeologist and undertook a formal investigation of the site. (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

After the teacher's discovery, a family member took the investigation further professionally.
questions.explanation: The teacher's **son** became an archaeologist. This is a factual detail question. In IELTS Listening Part 4, family relationships and professional roles are common detail items. 'Archaeologist' /ˌɑːrkiˈɒlədʒɪst/ = a person who studies human history through excavation.

questions.q: A traditional method used by local people to dig for ___ was used to identify where stones were located. (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

The investigation used a traditional local method to locate buried stones. This method was also used by local people for a common rural activity.
questions.explanation: Local people dug for **peat** /piːt/ — a type of soil made from decomposed organic matter, historically used as fuel in Ireland. The same probing method used to locate peat was adapted to find buried stones. Key collocation: 'peat bog', 'cut peat', 'peat extraction'.

questions.q: Items are well preserved in the bog because of a lack of ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

Items found at Ceide Fields are remarkably well preserved. The bog environment is responsible for this preservation.
questions.explanation: Preservation occurs due to a lack of **oxygen** /ˈɒksɪdʒən/. Bog environments are anaerobic (low oxygen), which prevents bacterial decomposition. This is a science-based vocabulary item. Key collocation: 'oxygen-free environment', 'anaerobic conditions', 'bog preservation'.

questions.q: Neolithic houses were ___ in shape and had a hole in the roof. (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

Neolithic farmers who lived at Ceide Fields built houses with a distinctive shape and a specific architectural feature.
questions.explanation: The houses were **circular** /ˈsɜːrkjʊlər/ in shape. Circular or roundhouse construction was typical of Neolithic settlements. The hole in the roof served as a smoke vent. Key vocabulary: 'roundhouse', 'circular dwelling', 'Neolithic architecture'.

questions.q: Neolithic pots were used for storage and to make ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

Neolithic innovations at Ceide included indoor cooking and the use of pots for a specific purpose beyond storage.
questions.explanation: Pots were used to make **cheese** /tʃiːz/. Dairy processing (including cheese-making) is one of the key Neolithic innovations evidenced at the site. Key collocation: 'dairy products', 'fermentation', 'Neolithic diet'.

questions.q: Each field at Ceide was large enough to support a big ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

The fields at Ceide were organised to support farming at a significant scale.
questions.explanation: Each field supported a big **herd** /hɜːrd/ of animals. 'Herd' refers specifically to a group of cattle or large animals. Key distinction: 'herd' (cattle/large animals) vs. 'flock' (sheep/birds) vs. 'pack' (wolves/dogs).

questions.q: There is no evidence of structures to house animals during ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

The fields were likely used to control where animals grazed. There is no archaeological evidence for sheltering animals during a particular season.
questions.explanation: There is no evidence of sheltering animals during **winter** /ˈwɪntər/. This implies animals may have grazed outdoors year-round or were managed differently. Key collocation: 'winter shelter', 'overwintering animals', 'seasonal farming'.

questions.q: One reason for the decline in farming was a decline in ___ quality. (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

Farming at Ceide Fields eventually declined. Two contributing factors are identified.
questions.explanation: There was a decline in **soil** /sɔɪl/ quality. Soil degradation is a well-documented cause of agricultural decline in Neolithic Ireland. Key collocation: 'soil quality', 'soil erosion', 'soil fertility', 'land degradation'.

questions.q: Another reason for the decline in farming was an increase in ___ . (Write ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.passage:
**Ceide Fields – Part 4 (Questions 31–40)**

The second reason for farming decline at Ceide Fields relates to a climatic or environmental change.
questions.explanation: There was an increase in **rainfall** /ˈreɪnfɔːl/. Increased rainfall in the region contributed to waterlogging and bog formation, which ultimately buried and preserved the fields. Key collocation: 'increased rainfall', 'climate change', 'waterlogged soil', 'bogland expansion'.
